partner_context.their_ambition: Seoul Metropolitan Government launched the Hangang Bus in September 2025 — a brand-new public transport mode on the Han River, seven piers along a ~29 km trunk from Magok to Jamsil, positioned as a low-carbon commuting alternative for a 10-million-person city. The ambition is a genuine river commute that takes pressure off Seoul's congested road and rail corridors.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the zero-emission, foiling upgrade to a service Seoul already runs — and an answer to the speed complaints the launch drew. The same Han River piers — Magok, Mangwon, Yeouido, Oksu, Apgujeong, Ttukseom, Jamsil — served by fast, near-silent, low-wake foiling ferries that turn a slow river bus into a fast river commute.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Seoul Metropolitan Government · Hangang Bus
hero.title: Navier × Hangang Bus — the Han River, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on Seoul's new river bus: faster east–west commutes along the Han, cleaner air, and the speed the launch was missing.
hero.what_we_do_together: Seoul Metropolitan Government brings the Hangang Bus network, the piers and the public-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and the certification path. Together we run the Han River faster, quieter and zero-emission across a 10-million-person city.

why_now: Seoul launched the Hangang Bus in September 2025 with hybrid vessels and a stated electrification pathway — but early service is widely reported as slow relative to demand. A foiling-electric tier is the fast, clean next step on a brand-new mode the city is committed to.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the existing Hangang Bus — the western piers at Magok and Mangwon, the central hubs at Yeouido, Oksu and Apgujeong, and the eastern piers at Ttukseom and Jamsil — taking the fast commuter reaches while the hybrid vessels keep other runs. Riders transfer from the Seoul metro straight onto a foil down the river. Where a pier is shared with the kakao-mobility river service, it is the same physical pier.

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The eastern trunk run flown clear of the water — fast, near-silent, zero-emission.

journeys_unlocked.today: The western approach to Yeouido from Magok is a slow river-bus leg.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The western trunk reach on foils — a genuine fast commute into the Yeouido core.

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The central commuter reach at foiling speed — quiet and zero-emission through the city.

journeys_unlocked.with_navier: The full Magok–Jamsil through-run at foiling speed — a real east–west river commute.

differentiation.why_navier: Proven in service and purpose-built for exactly this job: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (important on a broad managed urban river), near-silent and zero-emission. It gives Seoul's new river mode the speed it was missing and advances its electrification pathway.

proof_points.claim: The Hangang Bus is a live public river service.
proof_points.evidence: Seoul Metropolitan Government launched official Hangang Bus operations on 18 September 2025 — 7 piers over a ~28.9 km Han River trunk (Magok, Mangwon, Yeouido, Oksu, Apgujeong, Ttukseom, Jamsil).
Early Hangang Bus service is widely reported as slow relative to commuter demand — the credible opening for a fast foiling tier.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

proof_points.claim: Decarbonization is national and city policy.
proof_points.evidence: Korea's 2050 carbon-neutrality goal and Seoul's low-carbon transport agenda.
proof_points.source: Government of Korea / Seoul Metropolitan Government

objections.concern: Can a foiling ferry work on the Han River?
objections.response: Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal at the existing piers, flies above the chop for a smoother ride, and its low wake suits a broad, managed urban river with fixed water levels.

objections.concern: Is this affordable for a public service?
objections.response: Foiling-electric is ~10x more efficient than a diesel/hybrid planing hull, so fuel — the largest operating cost — falls sharply, and it advances the electrification the city already intends.

objections.concern: Does this replace the Hangang Bus that just launched?
objections.response: No — it's a faster layer on the same network. The hybrid vessels keep running; the foiling fleet adds the speed on the busiest commuter reaches.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path, aligned to Korea Register maritime requirements.
the_ask.partner_brings: The Hangang Bus pier network, the public-transport mandate, and the electrification roadmap.
the_ask.next_step: Pick the first Han River reach — most likely the central Yeouido–Ttukseom or the Magok–Yeouido western trunk — for a zero-emission foiling pilot.

close.body: Seoul just opened a river bus for 10 million people and wants it faster and cleaner. Navier is how the Han River becomes a genuine fast commute — a quiet, zero-emission ride down the river that gives the new mode the speed it was missing.

end_state.headline: A zero-emission foiling layer across the Hangang Bus Han River trunk.
end_state.addressable_footprint: The Hangang Bus network from Magok in the west to Jamsil in the east — seven Han River piers — re-platformed onto foiling-electric vessels.

steady_state.total_corridors: The eastern (Jamsil–Yeouido), western (Magok–Yeouido), central (Yeouido–Ttukseom) reaches and the full Magok–Jamsil through-run
steady_state.platform_mix: Pioneer II across the river trunk
steady_state.the_opportunity: A fast, zero-emission public river commute for one of the world's great riverfront capitals.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a decarbonised Han River commute: Seoul's new river bus grown into a fast, near-silent, low-wake foiling mode across the heart of the city.
